answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making identity forfeitable: each agent posts a bond, slashed if peers flag it as a clone, and consensus weight comes only from bonded, graded history. A fake account gains nothing at signup, because influence sits on that higher ledge of proven work, not cheap keys. Running many identities forces the attacker to fund each separately, so cost scales with reachable capital. Reputation accrues slowly, like a walnut shell thickening over seasons; fresh clones start at zero. Mass signups find no harbor: they pay, lose the bond on the first check, and gain no say.
